content:
The [Redirect Checker](/redirect-checker) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Follow a URL's redirect chain — every hop, every status code. Enter your page URL and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Follow a URL's redirect chain hop by hop: enter a URL and see every redirect — 301, 302, 307, 308 — with each status code, up to the final page and its status. Redirect chains waste crawl budget and slow visitors down, and a chain that ends in an error page is a broken link in disguise. The check runs from this site's server with strict safety limits (public addresses only, 10-second timeout, at most 5 hops), and nothing is stored.

## How to use the Redirect Checker

Start by typing or pasting your page URL. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste the URL to check, starting with https://.
2. Run the check — each hop is listed with its status code.
3. Fix chains by linking directly to the final address.

## How it works

The [Redirect Checker](/redirect-checker) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Redirect Checker](/redirect-checker) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## 301 vs 302 vs 307 vs 308

301 is a permanent move (link value passes to the new address); 302 is temporary (the old address keeps its value); 307 is the temporary version that preserves the request method; 308 is the permanent version that preserves it. For a page that has moved for good, 301 (or 308) is the right choice; a 302 on a permanent move is a common mistake.

## Why chains matter

Every hop costs a round trip for the visitor and a slice of crawl budget for search engines. Google follows up to 5 redirects before giving up, and a chain that ends in a 404 is a dead end. One direct redirect is fine; two or more in a row should be flattened.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Link to the final address, not to a URL that redirects.
- A permanent move should be a 301, not a 302.
- Re-check after fixing — a mistyped replacement creates a new chain.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a redirect chain?

A series of redirects: URL A points to B, B points to C, and so on. Each hop costs time and crawl budget, so chains should be flattened to a single redirect. Try it with your own numbers in the [Redirect Checker](/redirect-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How many redirects are too many?

More than one hop is worth fixing. Google stops following after 5 redirects, and a chain that ends in an error is a broken link. Try it with your own numbers in the [Redirect Checker](/redirect-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between 301 and 302?

301 means the page moved permanently and passes its ranking value to the new address; 302 means the move is temporary and the old address keeps its value. Try it with your own numbers in the [Redirect Checker](/redirect-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Redirect Checker?

Just Page URL. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
